churches.assessment: The United Church of Christ of Fredericksburg belongs to the most progressive mainline denomination in American Protestantism. The UCC was the first denomination to ordain an openly gay minister (1972) and the first to affirm same-sex marriage (2005). The denomination's 'God is still speaking' campaign and social justice emphasis define its institutional identity. While individual UCC congregations can theoretically be more conservative, the denominational DNA is thoroughly progressive. Rev. Darryl Moch leads. Not recommended for anyone committed to biblical authority and historic orthodoxy.

score_notes.gender: Male pastoral team (Jimmy Pruitt, Brian Mandel). No explicit complementarian or egalitarian statement found publicly. Max Lucado (Oak Hills origin) holds a more grace-forward, less structured complementarian position. Yellow until local stance confirmed.

score_notes.soteriology: Statement of Faith: 'Salvation is God's free gift, available to all who trust in Christ.' Faith-alone framing is strong. Note: 'Believers are called to repent, confess, and be baptized in response to the gospel' — baptism framed as response, not requirement for salvation. Correct.
score_notes.cultural: Values include 'Unity in the Body of Christ,' 'grace, truth and faith' — healthy evangelical framing. No DEI/CRT language visible. 'Inter-denominational' descriptor suggests openness across evangelical spectrum.
score_notes.preaching: Website offers sermon notes and 'Dig Deeper Resources' — encouraging for substantive teaching ministry. Style unknown (expository vs topical).
score_notes.mens_discipleship: No dedicated men's ministry found on website.
score_notes.denominational: Independent since 2019 launch; some informal accountability through Oak Hills relationship (Max Lucado) but no formal denominational oversight.

churches.assessment: Bridge Church Fredericksburg has one of the cleanest statements of faith among the churches surveyed: Trinitarian, Bible as final authority, salvation by grace through faith, baptism as response (not requirement), Great Commission-focused. The church was launched in 2019 by Max Lucado and the Oak Hills Church (San Antonio) team — Jimmy Pruitt was the former campus pastor who was invited by Max to take it independent. That's a vote of confidence from one of the most respected evangelical communicators of our generation. The two-service Sunday model with sermon notes and discipleship resources indicates a substantive ministry rather than a casual social gathering. Main watch items: no explicit complementarian statement, no formal denominational accountability, no confirmed men's ministry. The 'inter-denominational' description means Moop would need to probe the gender/leadership question directly before committing. Overall one of the more theologically promising independent churches in the FXBG area.

churches.assessment: St. Aidan's Anglican Church in Kansas City is an ACNA parish in the Diocese of the Upper Midwest, led by Rector Fr. Michael Flowers. The church was planted in 2012 in his home with a team of twelve. Fr. Flowers holds a B.A. in Theology from Oral Roberts University and a Master's in Theology from Fuller Theological Seminary, and reclaimed his initial calling to the Anglican priesthood during an extended sabbatical beginning in 2004 after moving to Kansas City. The parish maintains an unusually rich liturgical rhythm for its size: Sunday 10:00 AM worship plus daily (Monday-Friday) Morning Prayer Eucharist 6:45-7:15 AM. They host the 'Word and Table' podcast exploring Christian tradition. Meets at Nazarene Theological Seminary. ACNA 39 Articles framework with male-only ordination aligns with MOOP's rubric. Strong green-rated Anglican option for the Kansas City area.
